tagline: Through the Badlands wall on a road that lost its parent.
intro: Out of Wall, SD 240 heads south into Badlands National Park and turns southeast, its curves climbing through passes in the Badlands wall of pinnacles, buttes and mounds. A dozen roadside overlooks stand along the way. At Cedar Pass the road swings northeast and comes back to the interstate at Cactus Flat, about an hour of driving if nobody stops.

The Lakota named the country makȟóšiča, bad lands. The loop had gravel on it by 1944 and was signed for years as US 16 Alternate, until US 16 was cut back to Rapid City and the alternate had nothing left to be an alternate to.

moments.title: Wall
moments.text: A railroad town platted in 1907 and named for the rock wall of the Badlands, where a drugstore bought in 1931 made its name giving away ice water.

moments.title: Sage Creek Rim Road
moments.text: A gravel spur off the western end of the loop, where buffalo roam along the road and the standing advice is to drive carefully.

moments.title: Ben Reifel Visitor Center
moments.text: At the southeastern tip of the loop, a Mission 66 visitor center from 1957 and 1958 keeps a fossil preparation lab, and the lodge beside it sells the only food in the park.

practical: The road is two-lane and paved, with several steep passes and reduced speed limits in places, and it can close suddenly in winter or extreme weather. A national park entrance fee is collected on it.
